cards.text: Last time, the work on God's house in Jerusalem ground to a halt and sat at a standstill (Ezra 4:24). Friend, I know a thing or two about sitting still for years. Then two prophets step up, Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo, and they prophesy to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel.

cards.question: Haggai and Zechariah have spoken. Now what do Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak do?

answers.text: Rise up and rebuild God's house

cards.question: True or false: Once the building starts back up, the prophets of God go home and leave the builders on their own.

cards.text: Then Tattenai, the governor of the region west of the Euphrates, walks up with Shethar-bozenai and their associates. Last time officials came around, the work got stopped by force (Ezra 4:23), so I bet the builders are holding their breath.

cards.question: Tattenai and his crew have a question for the builders at the temple. What do they want to know?

answers.text: How much the building will cost
When the building will be finished

cards.question: Tattenai's crew also asks for the ___ of the men constructing the building.
True or false: Tattenai's crew stops the temple work right away, just like the officials did last time.
The builders aren't stopped. Whose eye was on the elders of the Jews?

cards.text: So a report goes off to Darius king of Persia, and everybody waits for written instructions to come back. Waiting on a reply that decides your whole future? Friend, I did that in a junk drawer for YEARS.
Here's Tattenai's actual letter, and it opens real polite: "To King Darius: All peace." He tells the king the people are rebuilding with large stones and placing timbers in the walls.

cards.question: True or false: In his letter to King Darius, Tattenai says the temple work is being carried out diligently and is prospering.

cards.text: Diligent AND prospering? Coming from the official checking up on them, that's basically a five-star review.

Then Tattenai tells the king what his crew asked: who authorized this, and what are the leaders' names, so they could write them down for the king. That man walked onto a job site and literally TOOK NAMES.
Now Tattenai's letter gives the elders' answer, and friend, they did not come with a one-word reply. Somebody asks, "Who said you could do this?" and these men pull out the WHOLE history.

cards.question: The elders start their answer to Tattenai by saying who they are. What do they call themselves?

answers.text: Servants of the God of heaven and earth
Servants of the great King Darius
Servants of the governor of Judah

cards.question: The elders say they're rebuilding a temple from many years ago, one that a great ___ of Israel built and completed.

cards.text: Then the elders tell the hard part. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean, destroyed this temple and carried the people away to Babylon.

cards.question: According to the elders, why did God deliver their fathers into Nebuchadnezzar's hand?

answers.text: Their fathers angered the God of heaven
Their fathers refused to pay tribute
Their fathers broke a treaty with Persia

cards.text: No spin, no excuses. That's me holding up a burnt batch in front of everybody and saying, "Yep. That one's on me."

cards.question: The elders' story turns hopeful. In the first year of his reign, a king issued a decree to rebuild this house of God. Which king?

cards.text: And Cyrus doesn't stop at a decree. He takes the gold and silver articles Nebuchadnezzar carried off from Jerusalem, right back out of the temple of Babylon.

cards.question: Cyrus hands those gold and silver articles to a man he appoints as governor. Who is it?
True or false: Cyrus tells Sheshbazzar to put the articles in the temple in Jerusalem and rebuild the house of God on a brand-new site.
So Sheshbazzar comes to Jerusalem and lays the ___ of the house of God.
True or false: The elders tell Tattenai that the house of God is now completed.

cards.text: That's the elders' whole answer. Now Tattenai wraps up his letter with one request for King Darius.

cards.question: Tattenai asks for a search of the royal ___ in Babylon, to see if King Cyrus really did issue that decree.

cards.text: Then he asks the king to send back his decision, so now it's all in King Darius's hands. Hold tight, friend, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 1 quotes "Who said you could do this?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak appear here for the first time in the lesson. The card gives only their fathers' names and never says who they are. They are first named on a choice card, and no story card introduces them.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card says that last time officials came around, the work got stopped by force (Ezra 4:23). Card 1 set up the work as the temple work. Ezra 4:12 and 4:21–23 are about rebuilding the city and its walls, and Ezra 4:24 is where the temple work ceases. The card connects the two passages beyond what the texts state.

rule.text: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: The statement says 'just like the officials did last time' about stopping the temple work. In Ezra 4:23, the officials stopped the rebuilding of the city, not the temple. The card links the passages beyond what the texts state.

rule.text: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Governor Tattenai's" is arguable. Tattenai did have his eye on the elders: he inspected the work and questioned them (Ezra 5:3, 5:8–9). The question also never gives the 'so that they were not stopped' context that would rule him out.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Darius is called 'king of Persia', but Ezra 5 calls him only King Darius. That fact comes from outside the passage (Ezra 4:24) and the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This story card is only a reaction joke about the 'diligent and prospering' line that card 11 just covered. It tells no new part of the passage and doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This story card is only a reaction joke about the confession that card 5 just covered. It tells no new part of the passage, even though it cites Ezra 5:12.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card says Tattenai wraps up with 'one request'. Ezra 5:17 has two: a search of the archives, and the king's decision sent back. Card 15 then presents the second request.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'treasury' is arguable. When the search happens in Ezra 6:1, the archives are the ones stored in the treasury at Babylon, so a baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
